_meta.about: One reasoning card per technique, written from the ATT&CK definitions of the techniques in the vendored table (data/attck_techniques.json); source names the table fields each card's head is checked against. requires: what the evidence has to show; kind: behaviour (the action alone is the technique) or intent (the action needs a stated adversarial purpose); indicators: what a reader looks for; siblings: techniques it is confused with and the criterion that tells them apart. Cards are shown to the models as reference beside a technique they named; nothing is decided from them.

T1003.name: OS Credential Dumping
requires: credential material is read from the operating system: LSASS memory, the SAM or SECURITY hive, the domain database or the shadow file
indicators: a handle opened on lsass.exe with memory read access
MiniDumpWriteDump on another process
hive saves of SAM or SECURITY

siblings.criterion: the secrets come from an application's password store (a browser, a keychain, the credential manager), not from the operating system
the credentials sit in files, scripts or the registry in plain form
the credential material is read from the LSASS process's memory in particular

T1005.name: Data from Local System
requires: files or data on the local system are read and gathered for the sample's use or to be sent out
indicators: reads over user folders
a list of targeted file extensions
archives built from local files

T1006.name: Direct Volume Access
requires: a volume or disk is opened as a raw device and read around the file system
indicators: a device path such as \\.\PhysicalDrive0 opened for reading
DeviceIoControl on a volume handle
file system structures parsed by the sample itself

siblings.criterion: the raw disk is written to destroy it

T1012.name: Query Registry
requires: registry keys or values are read
indicators: RegOpenKeyEx and RegQueryValueEx calls
reg query command lines
key paths under HKLM or HKCU

siblings.criterion: registry values are written or deleted, not only read
the keys read are of installed programs and the claim is about which software is installed

T1014.name: Rootkit
requires: an operating-system component is modified or hooked (a kernel driver, a system call table, kernel callbacks, API hooks)
the claim states what the modification hides
indicators: a driver loaded with NtLoadDriver or a kernel service
hooks on system calls or kernel structures
entries removed from process or file listings

siblings.criterion: artefacts are hidden with ordinary attributes or locations and no operating-system component is changed
the change is made below the operating system, in firmware or boot records

T1016.name: System Network Configuration Discovery
requires: the host's own network configuration is read: interfaces, addresses, adapters, routes, DNS, proxy or ARP
indicators: adapter and interface queries such as GetAdaptersAddresses or GetNetworkParams
commands that print interfaces, routes or the ARP cache
proxy settings read from the system

siblings.criterion: the listing is of live connections, not of the host's configuration
other hosts on the network are listed or looked up

T1018.name: Remote System Discovery
requires: other systems on the network are listed or looked up by name or address
indicators: host-listing command lines
NetServerEnum or DsGetDcName calls
ping or ARP sweeps over a subnet

T1020.name: Automated Exfiltration
requires: collected data is sent out by the sample's own logic, with no operator request for it
indicators: an upload routine run right after collection
files sent as soon as they are found

siblings.criterion: the data goes over the command channel on the operator's request
the transfer is tied to a time schedule

T1021.name: Remote Services
requires: the sample opens a session on another host through a remote service (RDP, SMB administrative shares, SSH, WinRM, VNC, DCOM)
indicators: connections to remote-service ports with credentials
use of administrative shares
remote sessions opened with valid accounts

siblings.criterion: files are copied to the other host and no service session is used to act there
the remote service is attacked through a flaw, not logged into
a remote access tool gives an operator the host

T1027.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
requires: the sample's code, strings, configuration or files are encoded, encrypted, packed or otherwise made hard to read
indicators: high-entropy sections or blobs
decode loops over stored data
strings built at run time

siblings.criterion: the victim's files are encrypted to deny access to them

T1027.002.name: Software Packing
requires: the executable is compressed or encrypted by a packer and restores its code when run
indicators: a packer stub or a known packer's section names
a very small import table beside high entropy
code restored into allocated memory at start

T1027.005.name: Indicator Removal from Tools
requires: the sample's own tooling was changed to remove what a detection matched (signatures, strings, names)
the claim states the change evades a detection
indicators: a tool variant with its detected strings removed
builds recompiled after a detection
names changed from a known version

siblings.criterion: traces left on the host are removed, not features of the tool

T1027.007.name: Dynamic API Resolution
requires: API addresses are found at run time, by name or by comparing a computed value against each exported function, instead of being imported
indicators: a walk of a loaded module's export table
GetProcAddress or LdrGetProcedureAddress called with computed names
few imports beside many APIs used

siblings.criterion: modules are loaded by name through the operating system and used as imported

T1029.name: Scheduled Transfer
requires: data is sent out at set times or intervals
indicators: a timer before each transfer
transfers only inside set hours

siblings.criterion: the transfer follows collection with no time rule
the claim is about the channel the data goes over, not its timing

T1030.name: Data Transfer Size Limits
requires: data is split into chunks of a fixed or capped size before it is sent
indicators: a send loop over fixed-size blocks
a cap on the size of each upload

siblings.criterion: the size of what is sent is not limited and only the channel is named
data is compressed or archived before sending, not split

T1033.name: System Owner/User Discovery
requires: the current user, the signed-in users or the machine's owner are identified
indicators: GetUserName or GetUserNameEx calls
user-identity command lines
session or token queries for the user

siblings.criterion: all accounts of the host or domain are listed, not the current user
the groups a user belongs to are listed

T1036.name: Masquerading
requires: a feature of the sample (its name, location, type, signature or metadata) imitates something legitimate
the claim states the imitation is meant to pass as legitimate
indicators: a copy under a system folder with a system file's name
a renamed system utility
an extension or icon that claims another file type

siblings.criterion: a signed system binary proxies the sample's execution and its name is not copied
the artefact is hidden from view and imitates nothing legitimate

T1036.005.name: Match Legitimate Resource Name or Location
requires: a name or location of the sample imitates a legitimate one (a system file name, a vendor folder, a service name)
the claim states the imitation is meant to pass as legitimate
indicators: a copy under a system folder with a system file's name
a vendor-looking folder or product name
a name one character off a system file's

siblings.criterion: a signed system binary proxies the sample's execution and its name is not copied
the legitimate-looking DLL name is what makes a legitimate program load it, so the name serves a hijacked load

T1036.008.name: Masquerade File Type
requires: the file's extension, header or content type claims one kind of file while it is another
the claim states the false type is meant to deceive a reader or a control
indicators: an executable with a document or image extension
altered magic bytes
a payload fetched as an image

T1041.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
requires: collected data is sent out
over the same channel the sample uses for command and control
indicators: collected data in the body of command requests
uploads to the command server
encoded data in request parameters

siblings.criterion: the data leaves over a protocol other than the command channel's
the data goes to a web service such as cloud storage or a paste site

T1047.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
requires: WMI is used to query or run something (the wmic tool, WMI COM classes, WQL)
indicators: wmic command lines
WQL queries over Win32_ classes
IWbemServices calls

T1048.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
requires: data is sent out over a protocol other than the command channel's (FTP, SMTP, DNS, ICMP, a raw socket)
indicators: uploads to FTP or mail servers
data carried in DNS queries
a second channel beside the command channel

siblings.criterion: the data goes out on the command channel itself
the data goes to a web service

T1053.name: Scheduled Task/Job
requires: a task or job is registered with a system scheduler (the Windows Task Scheduler, at, cron, systemd timers) to run code
indicators: schtasks command lines or ITaskService COM calls
crontab entries written
task XML files

siblings.criterion: the autostart is a Run key or a startup-folder entry
a system service is installed

T1053.005.name: Scheduled Task
requires: a task is registered with the Windows Task Scheduler to run the sample (schtasks, the Task Scheduler COM interface or a task file)
indicators: schtasks /create command lines
ITaskService, ITaskFolder or IRegisteredTask calls
task XML under the Tasks folder

siblings.criterion: the autostart is a Run key or a startup-folder entry
a system service is installed
the scheduler is cron

T1055.name: Process Injection
requires: code or data is written into another live process's memory
execution is started or redirected inside that process
indicators: OpenProcess with write access followed by VirtualAllocEx and WriteProcessMemory
CreateRemoteThread, QueueUserAPC or SetThreadContext on a thread of the target
a section mapped into the target

siblings.criterion: the code is mapped and run inside the sample's own process
a DLL is placed where a legitimate program loads it and nothing is written into a running process

T1056.name: Input Capture
requires: keystrokes or other input the user types (credentials in a prompt included) are captured
indicators: SetWindowsHookEx with a keyboard hook
GetAsyncKeyState polled in a loop
a fake prompt that asks for credentials

siblings.criterion: the clipboard is read, not typed input
the screen is captured
window titles are only listed

T1057.name: Process Discovery
requires: the processes on the host are listed or looked up
indicators: CreateToolhelp32Snapshot with Process32First and Process32Next
EnumProcesses calls
tasklist command lines

T1059.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
requires: commands or scripts are run through an interpreter (cmd, PowerShell, a Unix shell, a script host)
indicators: an interpreter started with a command line
script files written and then run
commands piped to an interpreter

siblings.criterion: a signed system binary proxies the execution

T1059.003.name: Windows Command Shell
requires: cmd.exe runs commands or a batch file
indicators: cmd.exe started with /c and a command line
batch files written and then run
commands piped to cmd.exe

siblings.criterion: the interpreter is PowerShell

T1069.002.name: Domain Groups
requires: groups of the domain and their members are listed
indicators: group-listing command lines with /domain
LDAP queries for group objects
NetGroupEnum or NetGroupGetUsers calls

siblings.criterion: the groups are the local host's
accounts of the domain are listed, not groups

T1070.name: Indicator Removal
requires: an artefact of the intrusion on the host (a file, a log, history, a registry value, a connection record) is deleted or altered
the claim states the removal hides the intrusion
indicators: the sample or its drops deleted after use
event logs cleared
timestamps altered

siblings.criterion: security tooling is disabled, unhooked or changed (hooks removed from system libraries, services stopped)
the artefact is hidden, not removed

T1070.004.name: File Deletion
requires: files the sample dropped, or the sample itself, are deleted
the deleted files are the sample's own or ones it left behind
indicators: the running image deleted through a rename or a delayed delete
dropped files removed after use
a command line that deletes a file after a wait

siblings.criterion: the deleted files are the victim's, to destroy data
Windows event logs are cleared, not files deleted
command history is cleared, not files deleted

T1071.name: Application Layer Protocol
requires: command-and-control traffic is carried in an application protocol (HTTP or HTTPS, DNS, mail, file transfer)
indicators: command requests built with an HTTP library
commands carried in DNS records
a command server's URL or host in the configuration

siblings.criterion: the channel is raw TCP, UDP or ICMP with no application protocol

T1071.001.name: Web Protocols
requires: command-and-control traffic is carried over HTTP or HTTPS
indicators: WinHTTP or HTTP request calls such as HttpSendRequest
URLs and a user agent string in the configuration
replies from a web server that carry commands

siblings.criterion: the channel is DNS queries and answers

T1080.name: Taint Shared Content
requires: content on a shared drive or repository is changed or planted so other users run it
indicators: files written to network shares
existing shared programs or documents modified

siblings.criterion: a tool is copied to one host for the sample's own use

T1082.name: System Information Discovery
requires: the host's operating system, hardware or configuration is read (version, name, architecture, locale, disks)
indicators: GetComputerName, RtlGetVersion or CPUID reads
system-summary command lines
volume or hardware queries

siblings.criterion: the language or keyboard layout is read to learn where the host is

T1083.name: File and Directory Discovery
requires: files or folders are listed or searched
indicators: FindFirstFile and FindNextFile loops
listing commands over user folders
extension filters over a folder walk

siblings.criterion: the contents of the files found are read and taken

T1090.name: Proxy
requires: traffic is relayed through an intermediate host or a chain of proxies
indicators: a SOCKS or HTTP proxy in the channel

siblings.criterion: one protocol is wrapped in another

T1095.name: Non-Application Layer Protocol
requires: command-and-control uses a transport or network protocol directly (raw TCP, UDP, ICMP) with no application protocol
indicators: socket calls carrying a custom message format
ICMP payloads that carry commands

siblings.criterion: the traffic is HTTP, DNS or another application protocol
the claim is about the port, not the protocol

T1102.name: Web Service
requires: a legitimate external web service (a paste site, cloud storage, social media, code hosting) relays commands or holds a dead drop
indicators: requests to a public service's API
commands read from a public post or file
a dead-drop address resolved from a public page

siblings.criterion: the service receives stolen data rather than giving commands

T1104.name: Multi-Stage Channels
requires: separate command channels with different servers or protocols follow one another
indicators: a first channel that returns the address of a second

siblings.criterion: several servers are tried in turn for the same channel

T1105.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
requires: a file or tool is brought onto the host from outside, over the network
indicators: a network read such as InternetReadFile followed by a file write

siblings.criterion: the file moves between internal hosts

T1106.name: Native API

indicators: calls into ntdll's Nt and Zw functions
direct system-call stubs

siblings.criterion: modules are loaded and their exported functions used

T1113.name: Screen Capture
requires: the screen or a window is captured, as images or as a recording
indicators: BitBlt from a screen device context
GDI+ image encoders after a capture
image files written at intervals

siblings.criterion: window titles are listed and no image is taken
a camera is recorded

T1123.name: Audio Capture
requires: the microphone or system audio is recorded
indicators: waveIn or Core Audio capture calls
audio files written

siblings.criterion: a camera is recorded
the screen is captured

T1125.name: Video Capture
requires: video is recorded from a camera or webcam, or through a video application such as a call service
indicators: avicap32 or DirectShow capture calls
camera devices listed before recording

siblings.criterion: the victim's screen is captured, as images or as a recording, and no camera or video application is used
only sound is recorded

T1132.name: Data Encoding
requires: data is encoded with a standard or custom encoding
the encoded data is command-and-control traffic
indicators: encoded fields in command requests
an encoding routine applied before each send
a custom alphabet table

siblings.criterion: the traffic is made to look like something else (junk, steganography, another protocol)

T1132.001.name: Standard Encoding
requires: data is encoded with a standard encoding (such as hex, MIME or a standard 64-character alphabet)

indicators: standard-encoded fields in command requests
a stock encoding call before each send

T1134.name: Access Token Manipulation
requires: an access token is duplicated, impersonated, adjusted or created to change the security context
indicators: OpenProcessToken with DuplicateTokenEx
ImpersonateLoggedOnUser or SetThreadToken

siblings.criterion: the elevation comes from bypassing User Account Control

T1136.name: Create Account
requires: a new local, domain or cloud account is created
indicators: NetUserAdd calls
account-creation command lines
the new account added to an administrators group

siblings.criterion: an existing account is changed

T1140.name: Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information
requires: the sample decodes or decrypts its own stored data, strings or payload at run time
indicators: a decode loop over an embedded blob before use
a decryption routine called on stored strings

T1197.name: BITS Jobs

T1204.name: User Execution

indicators: a lure document or file name
an icon or extension meant to be clicked
text that asks the user to enable content

siblings.criterion: a signed system binary runs the sample and no user action is shown

T1204.002.name: Malicious File
requires: a user opens a malicious file (a document, archive, shortcut or executable)
the claim states the user is lured into opening it
indicators: a lure document or file name
an icon or extension meant to be clicked
text that asks the user to enable content

siblings.criterion: a signed system binary runs the sample and no user action is shown
the claim is about the message attachment that delivered the file

T1210.name: Exploitation of Remote Services

indicators: exploit traffic toward remote-service ports
a flaw's name beside a scan of targets

siblings.criterion: the sample logs into the service with credentials
the flaw is in a local client application

T1218.name: System Binary Proxy Execution

indicators: a system binary's command line naming the sample

siblings.criterion: a program loads the module through LoadLibrary and no system binary proxies it

T1218.011.name: Rundll32
requires: the system binary this technique is named for loads the DLL and calls one of its exported functions
indicators: the named binary's command line with the DLL path and an export
a DLL with no other way to run than an export
the named binary as the sample's parent process

siblings.criterion: regsvr32 runs it
a program loads the DLL through LoadLibrary and no system binary proxies it
a user opens the file

T1219.name: Remote Access Tools
requires: a legitimate remote access tool is installed or used to give an operator the host
indicators: a remote-support product installed or launched silently
its configuration pointing to an operator's account

siblings.criterion: the sample's own implant talks to its server

T1480.name: Execution Guardrails

T1486.name: Data Encrypted for Impact

T1518.001.name: Security Software Discovery

requires: a protocol is used over a port other than its usual one
indicators: a web protocol on a port other than 80 or 443
a well-known protocol on a different port

siblings.criterion: the protocol itself is not an application protocol

T1572.name: Protocol Tunneling
requires: one protocol is wrapped inside another to carry it past controls
indicators: DNS or HTTP carrying another protocol's frames
an SSH or HTTP tunnel set up to a host

siblings.criterion: traffic is relayed through a proxy, not wrapped

T1573.name: Encrypted Channel
requires: traffic is encrypted (TLS or a cipher applied to the messages)
the encrypted data is command-and-control traffic
indicators: TLS or HTTPS for the command channel
a cipher applied to request bodies
a key used before each send

siblings.criterion: the victim's files are encrypted

T1573.001.name: Symmetric Cryptography
requires: traffic is encrypted with a symmetric cipher (a shared key)
the encrypted data is command-and-control traffic
indicators: a shared key applied to request and reply bodies
a cipher routine called before each send

T1574.name: Hijack Execution Flow
requires: the way a program finds and loads code (DLL search order, side-loading, PATH, service paths, COM) is used so the sample runs in its place
indicators: a DLL named like a legitimate one beside a signed program
PATH or service path entries that point to the sample first
a proxy DLL that forwards exports

siblings.criterion: the sample loads its own module on purpose

T1574.001.name: DLL
requires: a DLL is placed where a legitimate program loads it by name (search order, side-loading)
indicators: a DLL named like a legitimate one beside a signed program
a proxy DLL that forwards exports to the real one

siblings.criterion: an entry of the PATH variable points to the sample first

T1574.007.name: Path Interception by PATH Environment Variable
requires: a program is placed in a PATH directory searched before the real program's
indicators: a PATH entry changed to put a writable folder first
a program named like a system one in that folder

siblings.criterion: a DLL is placed where a program loads it by name
a path with spaces and no quotes is used

T1599.name: Network Boundary Bridging
requires: a network device or boundary control (a router, a firewall) is taken over to pass traffic between segments
indicators: changes to router or firewall configurations
NAT rules added on a boundary device

siblings.criterion: traffic is relayed through a proxy on a host
a host firewall is changed

T1608.name: Stage Capabilities
requires: the adversary places tools or content on infrastructure it controls for later use
indicators: payload URLs on adversary-controlled hosts
tooling uploaded to cloud storage before use

siblings.criterion: the claim is about acquiring the infrastructure

T1620.name: Reflective Code Loading
requires: code is mapped and run from memory inside the sample's own process without going through LoadLibrary
indicators: a PE image copied into allocated memory with relocations and imports fixed by the sample
execution jumping into newly allocated executable memory
no file written for the module that runs

siblings.criterion: a module is loaded from disk through LoadLibrary

T1622.name: Debugger Evasion
requires: the sample checks whether a debugging tool is attached to it
indicators: ProcessDebugPort or ProcessDebugFlags queries
reads of the process's debug and heap flags
trap instructions or timing tricks around them
a stated change in what the sample does after the check (it exits, waits or hides)

T1685.name: Disable or Modify Tools
requires: a security tool is disabled, stopped, unhooked or changed so it sees less
indicators: security services stopped or deleted
hooks restored in system libraries
tool settings changed through the registry or policy

siblings.criterion: traces are removed and no tool is changed
an exclusion is added to the tool
